speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; these symptoms suggest a potential neuromuscular issue. To better understand your condition, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details; the pattern of worsening with activity and improving with rest is very specific. Have you noticed any difficulty swallowing, drooling, or changes in your voice quality?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The fluctuating weakness that worsens with activity and improves with rest, combined with diplopia worsening on gaze, is highly characteristic. REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_receptor_antibodies. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray.
